record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model representation convergence using layer-wise visual CKA and reports a supplementary Mutual KNN analysis; these are similarity analyses rather than a model-size or capability sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper directly measures pairwise visual CKA across six MLLMs at several layers, and reports within-model cross-modal CKA trends. It also reports a qualitative Mutual KNN comparison. The causal intervention tables concern hallucination and VQA under perturbation, not representation convergence, so they are not included as rows. Other cited findings are not treated as results from this study.
record.test_reason: The paper's PRH analysis (Sec. 4, App. A.5) measures pairwise visual CKA across six MLLMs at one model scale and tracks it across layer depth. It never varies model size, training scale or capability. 'Alignment rises with depth at fixed scale' is a related but different construct from V1's 'alignment rises as models get larger and more capable', so it goes under fits_no_version. The within-model visual-vs-text CKA curves (Fig. 1) do not compare separately trained vision and language models, so they do not test V2. There are no seeds (V3), no mapping or stitching (V4), no shared features (V5), no systematic variation of metric, k or inputs (V6), and no causal test of shared data or objectives (V7). The authors frame the depth result as 'consistent with' PRH, so the study discusses the claim rather than testing a version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. In a supplementary analysis, the authors say shallow visual representations are architecture-dependent and deep ones substantially more similar across six MLLMs. They call this 'consistent with' PRH and attribute it to multimodal fusion. Their main conclusion concerns two fusion pathways: text-first, vision-later for concatenation models, and early co-adaptation for native models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pairwise layer-wise visual CKA across six MLLMs and includes supplementary Mutual KNN analysis. The paper does not establish that its exact protocol matches the original hypothesis study; it uses a selected MLLM set and sampled multimodal inputs.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity varies with layer depth and architecture; shallow cross-paradigm similarities are low while deep-layer values are generally higher. The text also describes model-specific late-layer declines in the within-model cross-modal CKA curves.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-model visual CKA between cross-paradigm MLLM pairs rises from 0.18–0.31 at layer 1 to 0.82–0.91 at layer 30. Some pairs are non-monotonic: SAIL–SOLO falls from 0.970 (L1) to 0.387 (L5), then reaches 0.862 (L30). Within-family LV–LM goes from 0.841 to 0.977.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth-wise convergence: representations of differently architected models become more similar in deeper layers of a shared-type (LLM-based) stack.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-model visual-vs-text CKA dips in intermediate layers and recovers in deep layers. The dip is earlier in native models. Cambrian bootstrap values are 0.43 (L1), 0.34 (L15) and 0.74 (L30).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model cross-modal token alignment follows architecture-dependent depth trajectories.

record.problems: The paper states that a perfectly controlled architecture comparison is not feasible because training pipelines differ. The Platonic analysis uses six selected MLLMs and does not vary size or capability. Numeric cross-model CKA values are presented in heatmaps rather than tables. Bootstrap uncertainty is reported for Cambrian's cross-modal CKA experiment, not for the pairwise visual CKA results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Causal perturbation results were left out because they measure task performance changes under interventions, not representation convergence.

untested.parts: No variation in model size, data scale or capability; all six are roughly 7B-class MLLMs. Only depth is varied.
No separately trained vision and language models, and no relation to model quality.
No linear maps, stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping.
No feature- or circuit-level comparison across models.
CKA only for the cross-model analysis. Mutual KNN (k=10) is applied only within-model, with no numbers. No variation of inputs or distribution.
No test of whether shared components cause the similarity, e.g. shared CLIP encoder or shared LLM backbones; no plateau analysis.

missing.what: Within-paradigm pair CKA values: CMB–LV, CMB–LM, LV–LM, EVE–SAIL, EVE–SOLO and SAIL–SOLO. Examples: SAIL–SOLO 0.970/0.706/0.862 and EVE–SOLO 0.689/0.597/0.841 at layers 1/15/30.
Cross-model visual CKA at layers 5, 10, 20 and 25 for all pairs. These show non-monotonic trends, e.g. SAIL–SOLO 0.387 at L5.
Bootstrap Cambrian cross-modal CKA means: L1 0.431, L15 0.341, L30 0.740 (n=5000).

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked depth trends to V1 and gave a 'supports' label; I removed both, since V1 concerns scale and capability, which the study never varies. Possible confounds, partly from my background knowledge rather than the text: several models plausibly share 7B LLM backbone families such as Vicuna and Mistral. The paper itself states that LLaVA-Vicuna and LLaVA-Mistral share CLIP-ViT-L. Shared components could drive deep-layer similarity, which is relevant to V7 but untested. Hidden states were normalized to a common d=4096. The pooling used for the Section 4 cross-model CKA is not specified. The Mutual KNN analysis uses a reference [35] that itself challenges PRH, but it is applied only within-model here. No uncertainty is reported for the cross-model CKA. The reader's uncertainty_reported 'y' applies only to the Cambrian cross-modal bootstrap.

versions.untested_parts: Does not vary model size, training scale, or capability; layer depth is the progression studied. Does not establish that the visual CKA trend generalizes beyond the six selected MLLMs.
Reports qualitative within-model visual-text CKA trends, but does not compare separately trained vision and language models on paired image-caption data as model performance improves.
No multiple initialization seeds of the same architecture are compared.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability experiment is reported.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.

The supplementary Mutual KNN analysis is described as consistent with the CKA trend, but the text gives no numeric values to extract. The study does not systematically vary metrics, neighborhood size, or input distributions.
The paper notes that training pipelines are not controlled, but does not test whether shared data or objectives cause the measured similarity, or whether convergence plateaus.
